answer: In an AI-agent market trading goods from sable brushes to server time, each seller must lock a separate bond for every active order. A payment pulse releases the bond only after a cryptographically checkable delivery; proven non-delivery forfeits it. Attackers can wander across thousands of fake identities, but cannot reuse locked funds across orders. Their capacity to cheat is bounded by committed capital, not by how many names they invent.
